message.content:
Build the BACKEND for a native Calendar + Tasks feature in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Prisma). It talks to the customer's SOGo CalDAV over the mail server and exposes server actions. Deps `tsdav` + `ical.js` are installed. READ first: `lib/calendar/types.ts` (the contract — do NOT change it), `lib/mail/imap.ts` (it exports `resolveMailbox(mailboxAddress?)` which does requireUser + ownership + returns the mailbox address + decrypted password — REUSE it for CalDAV auth), `lib/auth.ts`, and how `lib/actions-mail.ts` structures its "use server" actions + rate limits.

ONLY create/edit: `lib/calendar/caldav.ts`, `lib/calendar/ical.ts`, `lib/actions-calendar.ts`. Do NOT touch prisma/schema.prisma, lib/calendar/types.ts, lib/mail/*, or any app/component tree (the UI agent owns those).

**Auth for every action:** call `resolveMailbox(mailboxAddress?)` (from lib/mail/imap.ts) to get `{address, password}` scoped to the logged-in user's own mailbox — never let a user touch a mailbox they don't own.

**`lib/calendar/caldav.ts`** — a `tsdav` DAVClient factory: `serverUrl = CALDAV_BASE`, `credentials: {username: address, password}`, `authMethod: "Basic"`, `defaultAccountType: "caldav"`. Handle the self-signed/internal-IP TLS: SOGo's cert is for mail.nxeon.cloud but we connect to 10.20.0.10 — set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` appropriately OR pass a fetch/agent with `rejectUnauthorized:false` + `servername:CALDAV_TLS_SERVERNAME` (tsdav accepts fetchOptions). Provide helpers to fetch calendars, and to fetch calendar objects in a date range (`calendarQuery`/`fetchCalendarObjects` with time-range). ALWAYS handle errors cleanly.

**`lib/calendar/ical.ts`** using `ical.js` — parse an iCalendar string into our `CalEvent`/`TaskItem` shapes (VEVENT → CalEvent, VTODO → TaskItem; handle all-day DATE vs DATE-TIME, DTSTART/DTEND/DURATION, SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION/UID/ATTENDEE, VTODO STATUS=COMPLETED, DUE, PRIORITY). And BUILD iCalendar strings from `EventInput`/`TaskInput` (generate a fresh UID via crypto.randomUUID, proper VCALENDAR/VEVENT or VTODO with DTSTAMP). Times in UTC.

**`lib/actions-calendar.ts`** ("use server", only async exports) — implement, all `resolveMailbox`-guarded + rate-limited on mutations, returning the contract types:
- `listCalendars(mailboxAddress?): Promise<CalendarInfo[]>`
- `listEvents(rangeStartISO: string, rangeEndISO: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<CalEvent[]>` — across the user's calendars in that window.
- `createEvent(input: EventInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok:boolean; id?:string; error?:string}>` — PUT a new .ics object to the target calendar.
- `updateEvent(id: string, input: EventInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok:boolean; error?:string}>`
- `deleteEvent(id: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`
- `listTasks(mailboxAddress?): Promise<TaskItem[]>`
- `createTask(input: TaskInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok:boolean; id?:string; error?:string}>`
- `setTaskCompleted(id: string, completed: boolean, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`
- `deleteTask(id: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`
Validate inputs; never expose the password to the client.

CRITICAL: Do NOT run `npm run build`/`next build` (it races with the UI agent). Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files). Do NOT run git. Report the exact exported action signatures + the auth/security approach + how you handled the TLS-to-internal-IP.

content.text:
Backend for the native Calendar + Tasks feature is complete. Only the three allowed files were created; `types.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/mail/*`, and the app tree were untouched. `npx tsc --noEmit` (excluding tests) reports **0 errors**.

## Files created
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/calendar/caldav.ts` — tsdav DAVClient factory + fetch/PUT/delete helpers
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/calendar/ical.ts` — ical.js parse/build for VEVENT↔CalEvent and VTODO↔TaskItem
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-calendar.ts` — the `"use server"` actions

## Exported action signatures (match the contract exactly)
- `listCalendars(mailboxAddress?): Promise<CalendarInfo[]>`
- `listEvents(rangeStartISO: string, rangeEndISO: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<CalEvent[]>`
- `createEvent(input: EventInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok; id?; error?}>`
- `updateEvent(id: string, input: EventInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok; error?}>`
- `deleteEvent(id: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`
- `listTasks(mailboxAddress?): Promise<TaskItem[]>`
- `createTask(input: TaskInput, mailboxAddress?): Promise<{ok; id?; error?}>`
- `setTaskCompleted(id: string, completed: boolean, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`
- `deleteTask(id: string, mailboxAddress?): Promise<void>`

## Auth / security approach
- Every action begins with `resolveMailbox(mailboxAddress?)` (from `lib/mail/imap.ts`), which does `requireUser` + ownership check and returns `{ cred: {address, password} }` scoped to a mailbox the caller owns. The DAVClient authenticates as that mailbox (`authMethod: "Basic"`), so CalDAV enforces per-account isolation.
- Defense in depth: `createEvent`/`createTask` call `assertOwnedCalendar()` — the target `calendarId` must be one of the account's own collections, else a friendly error.
- The decrypted password is only ever passed into the DAVClient credentials; it is never returned to the client. Errors are normalized (`caldavError`, `cleanMsg`) and truncated so no stack/credential detail leaks. Mutations are rate-limited per user (burst 30/min + 600/hr) via the existing `lib/rate-limit.ts`, mirroring `lib/actions-mail.ts`.

## TLS to the internal IP
SOGo's cert is for `mail.nxeon.cloud` but we connect to `https://10.20.0.10/SOGo/dav`. tsdav uses the global (undici) fetch and forwards `fetchOptions` to it, so — instead of the process-wide `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` — I created a single module-scoped `undici` `Agent` with `connect: { rejectUnauthorized: false, servername: CALDAV_TLS_SERVERNAME }` and pass it as `fetchOptions.dispatcher` (cast, since `RequestInit` has no public `dispatcher` field). This disables verification only for this internal hop while still sending the correct SNI so the proxy selects the right vhost — the same pattern `lib/mail/imap.ts` uses for IMAP/SMTP. The Agent is reused across requests for connection pooling.

## Implementation notes worth relaying
- Events use a server-side `time-range` VEVENT filter (`fetchCalendarObjects` with `timeRange`); tasks use an explicit VTODO comp-filter (tsdav's default filter is VEVENT-only, so VTODO would otherwise be missed).
- All emitted date-times are UTC; all-day input emits `VALUE=DATE`. Parsing handles DTSTART/DTEND/DURATION (via `ICAL.Event.endDate`), all-day DATE vs DATE-TIME, SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION/UID/ATTENDEE (CN + mailto), and VTODO STATUS=COMPLETED/DUE/PRIORITY.
- `updateEvent` reads the existing object first to preserve its UID; `setTaskCompleted` mutates the existing VTODO body in place (status + percent-complete + completed timestamp) so other fields survive. New objects get `crypto.randomUUID()` UIDs and are stored as `<uid>.ics`; the returned `id` is the object's absolute href, used for later update/delete.
